edits.old:
We give the local argument behind the bimeromorphic ideal equivalence in \cite{SGPT}. For a local psh correction of $a$, let $a_m$ be its Bergman approximation of type $(1/m,\mathcal I(ma))$, with the smooth correction removed. Its lower bound is $a_m\geq a-C/m$ on smaller open sets by \cref{prop:bergman-local-estimates}.

Let $F:W\to Y$ be the composition of $\rho$ and any local modification with smooth source, and let $z\in W$. This is a generically one-to-one holomorphic map between manifolds of dimension $n$. Write $J_F$ for its local holomorphic Jacobian. For a germ $h\in\mathcal I(ma)$, change of variables shows that
\[
 |h\circ F|^2|J_F|^2e^{-ma\circ F}
\]
is integrable near $z$. The local radial integrability estimate then gives
\[
 \operatorname{ord}_z(h\circ F)
       \geq m\nu(a\circ F,z)-n-\operatorname{ord}_zJ_F.
\]
To see the estimate, use $a\circ F\leq(\nu(a\circ F,z)-\epsilon)\log|w-z|^2+C_\epsilon$ and the first nonzero homogeneous term of $(h\circ F)J_F$ on a set of angular directions of positive measure. Radial integrability forces its order plus $n$ to exceed $m(\nu-\epsilon)$; let $\epsilon\downarrow0$.

Apply this to finite local generators of the multiplier ideal. Together with the pulled-back Bergman lower bound it proves
\[
 \nu(a\circ F,z)-\frac{n+\operatorname{ord}_zJ_F}{m}
 \leq\nu(a_m\circ F,z)\leq\nu(a\circ F,z).
\]
If $a\sim_{\mathcal I}b$, the approximants at each integer $m$ have the same ideal type, so their pulled-back Lelong numbers agree. Letting $m\to\infty$ gives equality of the Lelong numbers of $a\circ F$ and $b\circ F$ at every such point. The local valuative criterion in \cref{thm:local-i-inputs} proves the forward implication.

For the converse take any real $t>0$ and a holomorphic germ $h$ on $Y$. Integrability of $|h|^2e^{-ta}$ near a base point is equivalent, by change of variables, to local integrability of $|h\circ\rho|^2|J_\rho|^2e^{-ta\circ\rho}$ near its fiber. Properness permits a finite cover of that fiber and a smaller base neighborhood, so these local integrals give the original one. Equality of the upstairs ideals at weight $t$ applies to the holomorphic germ $(h\circ\rho)J_\rho$ in each chart. It therefore gives the equivalent integrability with $b$ in place of $a$. This proves equality of the base ideals for every $t>0$.
edits.new: Apply the local order equivalence of \cref{lem:birational-ideal-order} to both $(a,b)$ and $(b,a)$. Its proof uses local Bergman estimates for the forward implication and proper change of variables for the reverse implication. It therefore applies in the present smooth setting without a compactness or closed-background assumption. The two order inequalities are exactly equality of the multiplier ideals at every positive weight.

\begin{proof}
Write $\varphi=\psi_D+v$ with $v$ bounded. Divisorial removal gives
$R=\theta+\ddc\varphi-[D]=\theta-\Theta_D+\ddc v\geq0$.
Its class is nef by \cref{lem:bounded-closed-potential-nef}.
If $\theta+\ddc\varphi\geq\delta\omega$ for a K\"ahler form $\omega$,
apply the same removal to $\theta+\ddc\varphi-\delta\omega$.
Then $R-\delta\omega\geq0$ still has bounded local potentials, so
$\{R\}-\delta\{\omega\}$ is nef. Adding the K\"ahler class
$\delta\{\omega\}$ shows that $\{R\}$ is K\"ahler.
\end{proof}

\Needspace{6\baselineskip}
Suppose $[\lambda]\in\mathcal C_X\cap(-\mathcal C_X)$. There are positive currents
\[
 T_+=\kappa_\lambda+\ddc u\geq0,
 \qquad T_-=-\kappa_\lambda+\ddc v\geq0.
\]
Their sum is $\ddc(u+v)$. Its mass against any fixed Gauduchon form $\gamma^{n-1}$ is zero by distributional integration by parts. Positivity forces $T_++T_-=0$, hence $T_+=T_-=0$. In particular $\kappa_\lambda=-\ddc u$. Taking a smooth Hermitian trace and applying elliptic regularity shows that $u$ is smooth, so $j_X([\lambda])=0$ in smooth Bott--Chern cohomology. The reverse inclusion follows because the zero class is pseudoeffective.
edits.new: By \cref{prop:psef-cone-compact-base}, the pseudoeffective Bott--Chern cone contains no nonzero line. Thus $j_X(\xi)$ and $-j_X(\xi)$ are both pseudoeffective exactly when $j_X(\xi)=0$. This is the asserted identity $\mathcal C_X\cap(-\mathcal C_X)=K_X$.
